desc: Next onboard kernel: CONFIG_MTD_PHRAM=y (added to T6040_ONBOARD_DEBUG's asserted set in t6040-kbuild.sh). m1n1 already publishes two reserved-memory nodes with compatible "phram": label adt (0x100040f0000 +0x94000) and label m1n1_stage2.log (0x105ce7a0000 +0x4000). With phram's OF support and the MTD char device (MTD=y, MTD_BLOCK=y today) they should appear as /dev/mtdN on every boot, giving the live ADT and m1n1's boot log without /dev/mem (STRICT_DEVMEM=y refuses RAM, confirmed by wallace-rex). Do not relax STRICT_DEVMEM. Read-only use only: never write, erase or mount the mtd devices (phram is writable RAM; a write would corrupt the ADT copy Linux and m1n1 rely on). Verify on the next onboard boot: cat /proc/mtd lists adt and m1n1_stage2.log; sha256 of /dev/mtd<adt> read twice is stable; the ADT header parses (wallace-rex tools/adt-dump.pl); m1n1 log readable. Rides on whatever kernel build comes next (no build of its own). Evidence: evidence/2026-10-30-t6040-device-map-live.md. ADDED 2026-10-30 (CJ decision, relayed by wallace-rex): CONFIG_PROC_KCORE=y in the same asserted set (not set on 5019, no /proc/kcore today). Purpose: read-only access to System RAM as an ELF core, for firmware-left data beyond the ADT. RAM only (no MMIO, no writes); STRICT_DEVMEM stays =y (CJ asked about disabling it; rejected for blind-MMIO SError risk, and kcore + phram is the agreed alternative). Same rule as phram: read-only, and no rig action derived from it without a ticket. Verify on the next onboard boot: /proc/kcore exists, readelf -l lists PT_LOAD segments for both RAM blocks (0x100032a8000.. and 0x10300200000..). Reading a no-map region (ramoops) is expected to be absent or zero.
